corrected_text: An EmbeddingGemma 2 vector at the full 768 dimensions in float32 takes 3,072 bytes; Agello's 768-dimension float16 vector (a691212) takes 1,536 bytes, half of it (512 bytes, a sixth, at the 256 dimensions it used until 2026-11-16).
note: Re-verified at Agello HEAD a691212 (read only). 768 x 4 = 3,072; 768 x 2 = 1,536 = 3,072 / 2; history 256 x 2 = 512.

corrected_text: Storing Agello's unit-length vectors (768 dimensions at a691212) as float16 changes a cosine score by at most about 2^-11 (~0.0005) per stored vector, since round-to-nearest float16 has a relative error of at most 2^-11 for normal values and sum |q_i d_i| <= 1 for unit vectors (subnormals add at most about 2^-25 per component).
note: Re-verified at Agello HEAD a691212 (read only). The bound doesn't depend on the dimension; VectorIndex.encode still rounds to Float16 (Embedding.swift:207-210) and vectors are unit length (normalize true, :66-67). The subnormal term per component is unchanged; summed over 768 components it stays far below 2^-11.

corrected_text: Because Agello a691212 sets no maxInputLength, its EmbeddingGemma engine loads signatures up to 1,024 tokens, so a passage or query plus its prompt prefix is read up to 1,022 SentencePiece tokens (1,024 with BOS and EOS); Agello asks LiteRT-LM to truncate a longer input rather than fail (inputOverflowStrategy .truncate), and its chunker sizes passages by estimated quarter tokens (1,600, about 400 tokens), not by the tokenizer.

corrected_text: In Agello a691212, KnowledgeBase.index embeds all passages of a document in one embed(documents:) call and, if it throws (outside the background), marks the document 'failed:<identifier>', which keeps it on keyword search and out of later indexing with that embedder until the user asks to index it again; KnowledgeBase.search indexes the documents in scope that need it, then ranks each document by meaning when it is indexed with the current embedder and its query embeds, and the others by keywords (BM25-style), interleaving the two rankings.
